items.title: Slovak, Hungarian PMs demand EU lift Russia energy sanctions

featured_image.name: Orbán calls for immediate lifting of sanctions on Russian energy

items.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico on Saturday called on the European Union to immediately lift sanctions on Russian oil and gas imports, restore flows through the Druzhba pipeline, and end the conflict in Ukraine to address the deepening energy crisis triggered by the war in Iran. The demand came after a phone call with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who issued his own warning that Europe faces a mounting energy emergency.[1]

items.title: Iran strikes Ben Gurion Airport, Gulf states with fresh drone and missile barrages

featured_image.name: Iranian forces claim responsibility for attack on Ben Gurion Airport

items.description: Iran's military announced Saturday that it carried out a large-scale drone attack on Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, striking several key facilities in what Tehran described as retaliation for continued American and Israeli military operations against Iranian territory. The strikes came as Gulf states absorbed yet another day of heavy aerial bombardment, and a drone hit one of the world's largest oil fields in southern Iraq.

items.title: Experts put odds of US ground operation in Iran at 85%

featured_image.name: War on Iran: What troops is the US moving to the Gulf? - Al Jazeera

items.description: As the US-Iran conflict stretches past its first month with no resolution in sight, military analysts and former combat pilots are raising alarms about the prospect of a ground invasion, warning that such an operation would be catastrophic in scope and risk repeating the failures of Iraq and Afghanistan.

items.title: Trump issues 48-hour ultimatum to Iran as downed airman search continues

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
President Trump on Saturday renewed his threat to unleash devastating strikes on Iran, warning in a Truth Social post that "all Hell will reign down" on Tehran if it does not make a deal or reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours. The ultimatum aligns with an April 6 deadline Trump set in late March, when he extended an earlier threat to destroy Iran's power plants by 10 days.[1][2][3][4]

"Recall when I allowed Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or REOPEN HORMZ STR. Time dwindling — 48 hours remain before all Hell breaks loose upon them," Trump wrote, adding "Glory be to GOD!" The warning reprises language from the president and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth threatening to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Age" and obliterate its power plants, oil wells, and desalination facilities.[5][6][3]

items.title: Over 40 nations demand Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: FRANCE-PROTEST-FUEL-TRANSPORT

items.description:
Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint that carried roughly 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption in 2024, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration — is rippling through economies from Brussels to Mumbai, reigniting inflation and forcing central banks into difficult policy choices.[1][2]

Iran closed the vital shipping lane to most vessels shortly after the United States and Israel began airstrikes at the end of February, according to Bloomberg. More than 40 countries met on April 2 to demand Iran unconditionally reopen the strait, while President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening escalation and claiming a deal is imminent.[3][4]

items.title: Adobe stock slides as alleged breach compounds CEO exit, downgrades

featured_image.name: Adobe CEO Shantanu Narayen is stepping down after 18 years—as ...

items.description:
Adobe shares have been battered in 2026, falling more than 27% year-to-date to trade near multi-year lows, as the planned departure of long-serving CEO Shantanu Narayen collides with a wave of analyst downgrades, a federal settlement, and an alleged data breach to create a perfect storm of investor anxiety.

The stock's decline accelerated in late March after William Blair cut its rating to Market Perform from Outperform, warning that intensifying competition "raises legitimate questions about what the future looks like for Adobe". That downgrade followed similar moves by Barclays, which lowered its rating to Equal Weight with a price target of $275, and Argus, which shifted from Buy to Hold — both citing uncertainty around the leadership transition. Earlier in March, Morgan Stanley had trimmed its price target from $425 to $365, triggering a sharp gap down in the stock.[1][2][3]

items.title: Zelenskyy invites US negotiators to Kyiv to revive peace talks

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy invites US negotiating delegation to Kyiv

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has invited a U.S. negotiating delegation to Kyiv in a bid to restart stalled peace talks with Russia, proposing the visit as an alternative to the trilateral format that has hit an impasse. The invitation, made public on Thursday, comes as Ukraine also presses for an Easter ceasefire that the Kremlin has already rejected.

items.description: Five weeks into the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, a growing consensus among analysts holds that Tehran is achieving its core strategic objectives despite absorbing devastating military blows — by raising the economic and political costs of the conflict beyond what Washington anticipated.

items.description: Israeli forces carried out fresh attacks across the Gaza Strip on Saturday, with gunfire, artillery shelling, and drone activity reported in multiple areas, according to Palestinian medical sources and eyewitnesses. The violence marks yet another day of hostilities in the nearly six-month-old ceasefire that has failed to bring lasting calm to the besieged territory.

items.title: IDF hits Iranian air defenses, missile sites in Tehran

featured_image.name: IDF strikes key Iranian air defenses, weapons development facilities ...

items.description: The Israel Defense Forces carried out a series of strikes on Iranian military infrastructure in Tehran on Friday, April 3, targeting air defense systems, ballistic missile storage facilities, and weapons research and development sites as the five-week-old conflict between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition showed no signs of slowing.

items.title: Trump gives Iran 48-hour ultimatum as search for downed pilot continues

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump issued a fresh 48-hour ultimatum to Iran on Saturday, warning that "all Hell will reign down" on the country if it does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or agree to a deal, setting up a Monday, April 6 deadline that arrives amid one of the most volatile stretches of the five-week-old war. "Remember when I gave Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT. Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!" Trump wrote on Truth Social early Saturday morning.[1][2][3]

The ultimatum lands as U.S. forces race to find a missing crew member from an F-15E Strike Eagle shot down over Iran on Friday — the first American aircraft lost since the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury on February 28. One of the jet's two crew members has been rescued, but Iranian state media reported a bounty of roughly $60,000 for anyone who hands over the second pilot alive. A second U.S. aircraft, an A-10 Thunderbolt, was also hit but its pilot ejected safely over Kuwaiti airspace.[4][5][1]

items.title: Meteor impacts may have created conditions for life, study finds

featured_image.name: Meteorite craters may be where life began on Earth, says ...

items.description:
The cataclysmic asteroid strikes that scarred the young Earth may have done more than reshape the planet's surface — they may have created the very conditions needed for life to begin, according to a new scientific review.

The paper, published in the Journal of Marine Science and Engineering, argues that hydrothermal systems formed in the aftermath of meteor impacts offered hot, mineral-rich environments where the first living cells could have taken shape. The research was led by Shea Cinquemani, a recent Rutgers University graduate, and co-authored with Distinguished Professor Richard Lutz, a veteran oceanographer who helped explore deep-sea vents decades ago.[1][2]

items.title: Leaked message undercuts Zarif's public peace plan for Iran-US war

featured_image.name: Iran foreign minister says will leave nuclear deal 'if necessary'

items.description: Former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif called on Tehran to "declare victory and make a deal" with the United States in a detailed essay published in Foreign Affairs on April 3, offering to curb Iran's nuclear program and reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief. But a leaked private message, published almost simultaneously, painted a starkly different picture — one of calls for military strikes on American ships and invocations of divine prophecy — raising sharp questions about the sincerity of his public diplomacy.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. intelligence warns Iran won't reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Hormuz chokepoint: Iran turns Larak Island into oil checkpoint

items.description:
Recent U.S. intelligence assessments warn that Iran is unlikely to reopen the Strait of Hormuz any time soon, as its stranglehold on the world's most critical oil chokepoint represents Tehran's only real leverage over Washington in the five-week-old war, according to three sources familiar with the matter cited by the Japan Times.[1]

The finding underscores a deepening crisis: rather than weakening Iran's hand, the U.S.-Israeli military campaign that began on February 28 may have inadvertently enhanced Tehran's regional influence by demonstrating its ability to paralyze a waterway through which roughly 20 percent of global oil supplies flow.

items.title: US doubles Hormuz insurance backstop to $40B but finds no takers

featured_image.name: Insurance Costs for Ships in Strait of Hormuz Rise Over 60%

items.description: President Donald Trump declared on Friday that the United States could "easily" reopen the Strait of Hormuz, writing on Truth Social: "With a little more time, we can easily OPEN THE HORMUZ STRAIT, TAKE THE OIL, & MAKE A FORTUNE. IT WOULD BE A 'GUSHER' FOR THE WORLD." The post came as his administration doubled its maritime reinsurance backstop to $40 billion and European nations pursued a diplomatic path that has so far resisted Trump's calls for allied warships to enter the waterway.[1][2]

items.title: Iran allows humanitarian ships through Hormuz but vows to keep control

featured_image.name: Which countries are allowed to cross the Strait Of Hormuz during ...

items.description: Iran on Saturday approved the passage of vessels carrying humanitarian and essential goods through the Strait of Hormuz, offering a limited opening in the waterway that has been effectively closed since the United States and Israel launched military strikes on the country on February 28. The move came even as Tehran declared it would never relinquish control over the strait, framing its grip on the chokepoint as a pillar of a reshaped global order.

items.description: Five weeks into the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, Washington's claim of overwhelming military dominance is running into a stubborn reality: Tehran's low-cost, dispersed strategy of attrition is raising the price of the conflict faster than American strikes can close it out.

items.title: Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire proposal, launches new strikes on Israel

featured_image.name: Israel targets Iran's Defense Ministry headquarters, Tehran unleashes  deadly strike

items.description: Iran rejected a U.S. proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire on Friday and pressed ahead with a fresh barrage of missiles and drones targeting Israeli military positions, deepening a conflict now in its fifth week with no diplomatic off-ramp in sight.

items.title: Gaza ceasefire talks end in Cairo with plans to resume next week

featured_image.name: Hamas says it will dissolve its Gaza government when new ... - The Hill

items.description: A two-day round of Gaza ceasefire negotiations in Cairo concluded on Friday in what sources described as a "positive atmosphere," with all parties agreeing to resume discussions in the Egyptian capital next week. The talks brought together a Hamas delegation led by Gaza chief Khalil al-Hayya, representatives of Palestinian factions, Egyptian officials, and international mediators from Qatar and Turkey.[1][2]

items.title: Iran's Ghalibaf taunts US after F-15E downed over Iran

featured_image.name: Is the US talking to Iran's Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, and ...

items.description: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf seized on the loss of a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle over Iran on Friday to taunt Washington, writing on X that American war aims had collapsed from "regime change" to a desperate search for downed pilots. The barb landed just two days after President Trump declared in a primetime address that the United States had "beaten and completely decimated Iran."[1]
